A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Beyond Scores: Proximal Diffusion Models with the same authors, core algorithms and convergence analysis. The main text, figures, equations and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix G report original sampling experiments on a discrete 2D distribution, MNIST and CIFAR-10, including generated samples, Wasserstein distances and FID results.

after.justification: The original experiments remain, supplemented by CelebA-HQ generation, MNIST/CIFAR-10 precision and recall, and controlled experiments on one-dimensional distributions in Appendix H.

M1.justification: The backward/hybrid updates, proximal-matching objective and conditioning scheme remain unchanged. Section 5 adds a limited adaptation for CelebA-HQ: the proximal model operates in a pretrained VAE's latent space, extending the original image-generation pipeline.

E1.justification: v2 retains the original datasets and adds CelebA-HQ at 256 × 256 resolution, extending evaluation to high-resolution face generation. Appendix H.1 also adds continuous, compactly supported 1D distributions with controlled boundary smoothness, distinct from the retained discrete 2D example.

E2.justification: The retained comparisons use the same Euler-Maruyama score SDE, final-denoising variants in the 2D experiment, and Euler probability-flow ODE methods. The new experiments reuse these comparator methods. Newly discussed accelerated samplers, consistency models and distillation methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Original MNIST/CIFAR-10 training budgets, schedules and step candidates are retained. v2 adds VGG-16-based precision/recall evaluation, CelebA-HQ FID over 30,000 generated samples, and a controlled 1D design varying five smoothness parameters across 5, 10 and 100 steps. These substantially broaden the evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: New Appendix H.1 and Figure 8 systematically test how boundary smoothness affects density and support recovery, comparing hybrid ProxDM with Euler-Maruyama without final denoising. This adds a substantial examination of the method's motivating premise. The existing CIFAR-10 training-heuristic ablation is retained as Figure 9, formerly Figure 6.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for the experiments. The added metrics and CelebA-HQ sample count do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Existing result plots are retained. New results show better support recovery in the 1D tests and CelebA-HQ FID competitive with score ODE and generally better than score SDE. Figure 10 adds precision/recall findings with important exceptions: CIFAR-10 precision favors score ODE at moderate and high step counts despite ProxDM's recall advantage over much of the range.

T1.justification: Section 2 corrects Tweedie's conditional-mean expression and noise scale, the sign in the MAP-proximal identity, and its Gaussian-likelihood derivation. Theorem 1 and Corollary 1 change the backward side condition from h ≤ 2 to h ≤ 1. The convergence rates, formal assumptions and appendix proof framework are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: backward and hybrid proximal diffusion, learning proximal operators through proximal matching, the exact-proximal convergence rate, and faster few-step sampling than conventional score methods. Added experiments do not redefine these main claims.

C2.justification: New Appendix A discusses the unresolved connection to maximum-likelihood training and attributes large-step FID deterioration to accumulated approximate-proximal errors. v2 also gives substantive qualifications about comparing convergence rates across assumptions and interprets the smoothness experiment cautiously. These significantly expand the original limitations and mechanism discussion.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository pointer, explicit training pseudocode in Algorithm 2, the precision/recall computation procedure and the CelebA-HQ FID sample count. Original training hyperparameters remain, while Section 3.3 condenses some explicit MLP/embedding details. The PDF establishes the code pointer, not the repository's contents or accessibility.

R1.justification: New Appendix A.1 substantially expands positioning against accelerated solvers, consistency models, distillation, flow matching and shortcut models. It presents proximal discretization as complementary to these approaches and connects proximal matching to MAP-promoting losses, adding works such as Song et al. (2023), Lipman et al. (2023), Frans et al. (2025) and Geng et al. (2025).

P1.justification: Most main exposition and proof organization remain intact. v2 makes localized rewrites, expands the loss explanation, introduces discussion subsections, improves appendix cross-references and switches to author-year citations. The new scientific content does not entail a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adds substantial visual material: CelebA-HQ sample grids and FID curves, a loss-function illustration, the smoothness comparison, precision/recall panels and a training algorithm box. Existing figures are retained or relocated; notably, v1 Figures 5 and 6 become v2 Figures 7 and 9.

improvement.justification: v1's empirical support was concentrated on a toy distribution and low-resolution images, with image quality assessed mainly through FID. v2 substantially strengthens that evidence through high-resolution generation, separate fidelity/coverage measurements and controlled support-recovery tests. Mathematical corrections and the explanation of large-step deterioration further improve reliability and interpretation. Comparisons still use basic Euler samplers and the theory still assumes exact proximals, but the expanded validation addresses important gaps in the earlier paper.
